prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a kitchen counter angled in front of and below the camera wearer in frames 1–3, shifting in frames 4–5 as the wearer turns right and tilts downward toward the floor (~1.0–1.5 m below) between the counter edge on the left and a second person standing on the right. In frames 1–3, the wearer's hands and a mesh bag of green beans are brightest and nearest at ~0.3–0.5 m in the lower foreground (within the wearer's arm's reach), while a sink and green cloth on the left, a white bag and lemons (~0.2–0.4 m apart on the counter surface) at ~0.6–0.9 m, and a paper towel roll, canister, mug, and coffee maker at ~0.8–1.2 m sit further back alongside a second person's right arm reaching in from the lower right (~0.5–0.7 m away and within arm's reach of the counter items). As the wearer turns right in frame 4 and looks down in frame 5, the second person's torso enters the right foreground at ~0.4–0.6 m (partially cropped by the right frame edge and occluding the background wall) before both the wearer's right arm and the second person's left arm extend downward toward a black-and-white dog on the floor (~0.8–1.2 m away, ~0.3 m from the cabinet base), with both people's heads out of view so gaze toward the wearer is not visible. The depth map clarifies the 3D relief of counter objects, the receding floor plane in frame 4, and the vertical separation between the raised counter edge and the dog below in frame 5, which is harder to judge in the dark RGB shadows. However, the map is unreliable inside the open mesh bag in frames 2–3 (flattening the interior hollow to the same depth as the rim), across the dark upper-left background in frames 1–2 (clamped to pure black), and in frame 5 where the angled wooden cabinet on the left appears artificially bright (~0.2–0.4 m) and blurred into the foreground.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map sparsely labels regions of the kitchen counter scene in frames 1–3 and the rightward turn toward the floor in frames 4–5, isolating foreground arms at ~0.3–0.7 m and mid-range counter items at ~0.6–1.0 m while leaving most of the background, coffee maker, lemons, and floor unsegmented black. In frames 1–3, it segments the cylindrical canister/mug at ~0.8 m in the upper center as `cup` and separates the camera wearer's foreground hands holding the bag (~0.3–0.5 m, lower left/center) from the second person's arm entering from the lower right (~0.5–0.7 m, ~0.2–0.3 m to the right of the wearer's right hand) as distinct `person` masks, though neither person's head or face is in view to indicate gaze direction. Across frames 3–5, as the camera turns right and downward, a large `person` mask in frame 4 captures the second person's torso on the right at ~0.4–0.6 m (facing left toward the counter and dog, partially out of view on the right and occluding the trash bin behind them), while both people's arms reach within arm's reach of the counter in frames 1–3 and toward the dog on the floor in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the segmentation map explicitly disambiguates the boundary between the wearer's right hand/arm and the second person's adjacent arm in frames 1 and 3 and isolates the second person's dark-clothed torso from the dark floor shadow in frame 4. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labeling and temporal consistency: it mislabels the green cloth at ~0.7 m left as `banana` (frames 2–3), the counter surface as `dining table` (frame 3), the counter and wall in frame 4 as `remote`, the green beans as `broccoli` (frame 4), and the counter/cabinet and upper wall in frames 4–5 as `banana`, while completely missing the dog, coffee maker, and both people's hands in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the 5-frame sequence, detecting only three isolated right-hand skeletons (magenta, at the bottom right of frames 1, 2, and 3) and a single misoriented torso/limb skeleton (yellow, over the counter in frame 2), while failing to capture the overall room layout, objects, or the dog. In frames 1–3, the magenta hand skeletons localize the second person's right hand resting at the right edge of the counter (~0.5–0.7 m from the camera wearer and ~0.2–0.3 m right of the wearer's hands), within arm's reach of the lemons and the mesh bag, with the rest of the second person's body occluded or out of the right frame boundary. Across frames 1–3, this detected hand shifts slightly leftward and upward relative to the bottom-right corner as the camera wearer's viewpoint adjusts, and in frames 4–5 all hand and body skeletons disappear completely except for a spurious magenta hand cluster on the middle-right background wall in frame 5. When cross-referenced with the RGB image, the magenta keypoints in frames 1–3 make the finger articulation and orientation of the second person's partially cropped right hand clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB corner, confirming the hand is angled leftward onto the counter surface. Nevertheless, the pose map is largely unreliable: it completely misses the camera wearer's own foreground hands (~0.3–0.5 m) in all five frames and both people's reaching arms in frames 4–5, hallucinates a horizontally oriented yellow body skeleton (with facial keypoints facing right) across the inanimate bags and canister on the counter in frame 2 (~0.6–0.9 m away), and places a false-positive hand skeleton on the bare wall in frame 5.
